title: Doors
tagline: Every door is shut. Teach the doors when to open, close and lock.
briefing: Every room on the Meridian has one door onto the central corridor. To change rooms, a crew member walks out through one door and in through another, and spends a moment in each doorway.

Right now every door stays shut, so nobody can go anywhere. The ship calls `nextDoorState(door)` for every door, twice a second, and sets the door to whatever you return: `"open"`, `"closed"` or `"locked"`.
A door isn't a yes/no like a light. It has three **states**, and what it should do next depends on what it is now.
starter: // The ship calls this for every door, twice a second.
//   { room: "Cargo", state: "closed", waiting: 1, inDoorway: 0, breach: false }
// state:     what the door is now: "open", "closed" or "locked"
// waiting:   how many crew are standing at the door, wanting to go through
// inDoorway: how many crew are in the doorway right now
// breach:    true if the room has a hull breach
// Return what the door should be next: "open", "closed" or "locked".

steps.title: Let people through
text: Look at the ship: crew with a pulsing yellow ring are stuck at a door, and the **Crew waiting** gauge keeps climbing.
Open a door when someone is waiting at it, and close it otherwise. You return the state as a **string**, and it has to be spelled exactly the way the ship spells it.

predict.question: Your function returns `"Open"`, with a capital O. What does the ship do?
options: Reports an error: it only knows `"open"`, `"closed"` and `"locked"`
predict.explain: Strings are compared exactly (remember `"bridge" === "Bridge"` from Lights). The ship doesn't guess what you meant: an unknown state is an error, and the door stays as it was.

goal.text: Doors open for anyone waiting and close when nobody is.

cases.label: Haddad at the Cargo door
cases.why: Someone is waiting, so open up.

cases.label: Nobody around
cases.why: Nobody needs the door: keep it closed.

cases.label: Two at the Galley door
cases.why: Two waiting is still "more than zero".

hints: It's the same shape as `lightOn`, but returning strings instead of `true`/`false`.

steps.title: Never close on someone
text: People can move now, but watch the log and the **Closed on crew** gauge. The moment someone steps into the doorway they're no longer *waiting*, so your code closes the door, on them.
Keep the door open while someone is waiting **or** someone is in the doorway. `||` means *or*: `a || b` is `true` if either side is.

predict.question: `door.waiting` is `0` and `door.inDoorway` is `1`. What is `door.waiting > 0 || door.inDoorway > 0`?
predict.explain: `false || true` is `true`: one side is enough. (`&&`, which you used in the power plan, needs both.)

goal.text: Doors stay open while anyone is waiting or in the doorway.

cases.label: Lin in the Med bay doorway
Nobody around
cases.why: Still close doors nobody is using.

hints: Only the condition of your `if` changes.
You want: waiting is more than zero, *or* inDoorway is more than zero.

steps.title: Seal the breach
text: Wait for a **hull breach** (the room flashes red and the log shouts). Someone always goes to check on it, your door opens for them, right onto the breach. Air rushes out (the **Air** and **Breach calls** gauges) and they're nearly pulled into space.
A breached room's door must be `"locked"`, no matter who is waiting. Like the emergency rule in Lights, the most important rule goes **first**.

predict.question: With the breach check at the top, Haddad is waiting at a breached door. What does the door do?
options: Closes now, then opens next tick
predict.explain: The first `return` that runs decides. The breach check runs first and returns `"locked"`, so the waiting check is never reached.

goal.text: Breached rooms are locked off, whoever is waiting.

cases.label: Breach, nobody around
cases.why: Locked, not just closed: nobody may open it.

hints: Put it on the first lines of the function, before the waiting check.

steps.title: Locked, then closed, then open
text: When a breach is repaired the room is safe again. But watch the **Seals torn** gauge: the person waiting outside makes your code open the door *straight from* `"locked"`, and that tears the door's pressure seal.
Ship rule: a locked door must spend a moment `"closed"` before it may open. This is your first **state machine**: what a door does next depends on what it is *now*, `door.state`.
Add the rule right after the breach check.

predict.question: The breach is over and Okafor is waiting at the locked door. With all four rules, what happens over the next two ticks?
predict.explain: Tick 1: no breach, the state is `"locked"`, so it becomes `"closed"`. Tick 2: the state is `"closed"` and Okafor is waiting, so it becomes `"open"`. Each tick looks only at the current state and moves one step.

goal.text: A locked door goes to closed before it can open.

cases.label: Breach repaired, Okafor waiting
cases.why: Locked must pass through closed first.

cases.label: Still breached
cases.why: The breach rule still comes first.

hints: If it is locked (and there's no breach), return `"closed"`.
Put it below the breach check, above the waiting check.

check.text: Doors all over the ship, in every situation. Each must choose the right next state.

cases.label: Med bay, Lin mid-doorway
cases.why: Never close on someone in the doorway.

cases.label: Bridge, breach repaired, pilot waiting
cases.why: Locked must pass through closed first.

cases.label: Cargo still breached, two waiting
cases.why: Stays locked until the breach is fixed.

concepts: the current state decides the next
